    def update_diet(
    self, prey_biomass: np.ndarray, predator_idx: Optional[int] = None
) -> "np.ndarray | None":
    """Update diet preferences based on prey availability.

    Uses a prey switching model where diet preferences shift toward
    more abundant prey species.

    Parameters
    ----------
    prey_biomass : np.ndarray
        Current biomass of all prey groups
    predator_idx : int, optional
        Update only this predator (None = update all)

    Returns
    -------
    np.ndarray
        Updated diet matrix

    Notes
    -----
    The prey switching model:

    new_diet[prey, pred] = base_diet[prey, pred] * (biomass[prey] / B_ref[prey])^power

    Then normalize so sum of diet = 1 for each predator.

    Higher switching_power = stronger response to biomass changes.
    """
    if not self.enabled:
        return None

    if self.base_diet is None:
        return self.current_diet

    n_prey, n_pred = self.base_diet.shape
    new_diet = self.current_diet.copy()

    # Calculate relative prey availability
    # Only use first n_prey entries (matching diet matrix)
    prey_biomass_subset = prey_biomass[:n_prey]
    prey_availability = np.maximum(prey_biomass_subset, self.min_proportion)

    # Update diet for specified predator(s)
    pred_range = range(n_pred) if predator_idx is None else [predator_idx]

    for pred in pred_range:
        # Get base diet for this predator
        base_prefs = self.base_diet[:, pred]

        # Only update where there's a base preference
        active_prey = base_prefs > self.min_proportion

        if not np.any(active_prey):
            continue

        # Apply prey switching model
        # new_pref = base_pref * (availability)^power
        new_prefs = base_prefs.copy()
        new_prefs[active_prey] = base_prefs[active_prey] * np.power(
            prey_availability[active_prey]
            / np.mean(prey_availability[active_prey]),
            self.switching_power,
        )

        # Ensure minimum proportions
        new_prefs = np.maximum(new_prefs, self.min_proportion)

        # Normalize to sum to 1
        total = np.sum(new_prefs)
        if total > 0:
            new_diet[:, pred] = new_prefs / total

    self.current_diet = new_diet
    return new_diet

    @dataclass
class ForcingFunction:
    """Single forcing function for a state variable.

    Attributes
    ----------
    group_idx : int
        Index of group to force (-1 for all groups)
    variable : StateVariable
        Which state variable to force
    mode : ForcingMode
        How to apply the forcing
    time_series : np.ndarray
        Time series of forced values (years)
    years : np.ndarray
        Year indices corresponding to time_series
    interpolate : bool
        Whether to interpolate between annual values
    active : bool
        Whether this forcing is currently active
    """

    group_idx: int
    variable: StateVariable
    mode: ForcingMode
    time_series: np.ndarray
    years: np.ndarray
    interpolate: bool = True
    active: bool = True

    def get_value(self, year: float) -> float:
        """Get forced value at given year (with interpolation).

        Parameters
        ----------
        year : float
            Simulation year (can be fractional for monthly time steps)

        Returns
        -------
        float
            Forced value at this time
        """
        if not self.active:
            return np.nan

        # Check if year is in range
        if year < self.years[0] or year > self.years[-1]:
            # Outside range - return NaN (no forcing)
            return np.nan

        if self.interpolate:
            # Linear interpolation
            return np.interp(year, self.years, self.time_series)
        else:
            # Use nearest year
            idx = np.argmin(np.abs(self.years - year))
            return self.time_series[idx]

    @dataclass
class StateForcing:
    """Collection of forcing functions for state variables.

    Attributes
    ----------
    functions : list[ForcingFunction]
        List of individual forcing functions
    """

    functions: List[ForcingFunction] = field(default_factory=list)

    def add_forcing(
        self,
        group_idx: int,
        variable: Union[str, StateVariable],
        time_series: Union[np.ndarray, pd.Series, Dict[int, float]],
        years: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
        mode: Union[str, ForcingMode] = ForcingMode.REPLACE,
        interpolate: bool = True,
    ):
        """Add a forcing function.

        Parameters
        ----------
        group_idx : int
            Index of group to force
        variable : str or StateVariable
            Which state variable to force
        time_series : array-like or dict
            Time series of forced values
            If dict, keys are years and values are forced values
        years : array-like, optional
            Year indices (required if time_series is array)
        mode : str or ForcingMode
            How to apply forcing ("replace", "add", "multiply", "rescale")
        interpolate : bool
            Whether to interpolate between annual values

        Examples
        --------
        >>> forcing = StateForcing()
        >>> # Force phytoplankton biomass to observed series
        >>> forcing.add_forcing(
        ...     group_idx=0,
        ...     variable='biomass',
        ...     time_series={2000: 15.0, 2001: 18.0, 2002: 16.0},
        ...     mode='replace'
        ... )
        >>>
        >>> # Add recruitment pulse for herring in 2005
        >>> forcing.add_forcing(
        ...     group_idx=3,
        ...     variable='recruitment',
        ...     time_series={2005: 2.5},  # 2.5x normal recruitment
        ...     mode='multiply'
        ... )
        """
        # Convert variable to enum
        if isinstance(variable, str):
            variable = StateVariable(variable.lower())

        # Convert mode to enum
        if isinstance(mode, str):
            mode = ForcingMode(mode.lower())

        # Handle dict input
        if isinstance(time_series, dict):
            years = np.array(list(time_series.keys()))
            time_series = np.array(list(time_series.values()))
        elif isinstance(time_series, pd.Series):
            years = time_series.index.values
            time_series = time_series.values
        else:
            time_series = np.asarray(time_series)

        if years is None:
            raise ValueError("years must be provided if time_series is not a dict")

        years = np.asarray(years)

        # Create forcing function
        func = ForcingFunction(
            group_idx=group_idx,
            variable=variable,
            mode=mode,
            time_series=time_series,
            years=years,
            interpolate=interpolate,
            active=True,
        )

        self.functions.append(func)

    def get_forcing(
        self, year: float, variable: StateVariable, group_idx: Optional[int] = None
    ) -> List[Tuple[ForcingFunction, float]]:
        """Get all active forcing values for a variable at given time.

        Parameters
        ----------
        year : float
            Current simulation year
        variable : StateVariable
            Which state variable to query
        group_idx : int, optional
            Specific group index (None = all groups)

        Returns
        -------
        list of (ForcingFunction, float)
            List of (forcing function, forced value) tuples
        """
        results = []

        for func in self.functions:
            if not func.active or func.variable != variable:
                continue

            # Check if this forcing applies to the group
            if group_idx is not None:
                if func.group_idx != -1 and func.group_idx != group_idx:
                    continue

            value = func.get_value(year)
            if not np.isnan(value):
                results.append((func, value))

        return results

    def remove_forcing(self, group_idx: int, variable: Union[str, StateVariable]):
        """Remove forcing for a specific group and variable.

        Parameters
        ----------
        group_idx : int
            Index of group
        variable : str or StateVariable
            Which state variable
        """
        if isinstance(variable, str):
            variable = StateVariable(variable.lower())

        self.functions = [
            f
            for f in self.functions
            if not (f.group_idx == group_idx and f.variable == variable)
        ]

    def create_biomass_forcing(
    group_idx: int,
    observed_biomass: Union[np.ndarray, pd.Series, Dict[int, float]],
    years: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
    mode: str = "replace",
    interpolate: bool = True,
) -> StateForcing:
    """Convenience function to create biomass forcing.

    Parameters
    ----------
    group_idx : int
        Index of group to force
    observed_biomass : array-like or dict
        Observed biomass time series
    years : array-like, optional
        Year indices
    mode : str
        Forcing mode ("replace", "add", "multiply")
    interpolate : bool
        Whether to interpolate monthly values

    Returns
    -------
    StateForcing
        Forcing object ready to use

    Examples
    --------
    >>> # Force phytoplankton to observed biomass
    >>> forcing = create_biomass_forcing(
    ...     group_idx=0,
    ...     observed_biomass={2000: 15.0, 2005: 18.0, 2010: 16.0},
    ...     mode='replace'
    ... )
    """
    forcing = StateForcing()
    forcing.add_forcing(
        group_idx=group_idx,
        variable=StateVariable.BIOMASS,
        time_series=observed_biomass,
        years=years,
        mode=mode,
        interpolate=interpolate,
    )
    return forcing

    def create_recruitment_forcing(
    group_idx: int,
    recruitment_multiplier: Union[np.ndarray, Dict[int, float]],
    years: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
    interpolate: bool = False,
) -> StateForcing:
    """Convenience function to create recruitment forcing.

    Parameters
    ----------
    group_idx : int
        Index of group to force
    recruitment_multiplier : array-like or dict
        Recruitment multiplier (1.0 = normal, 2.0 = double, etc.)
    years : array-like, optional
        Year indices
    interpolate : bool
        Whether to interpolate (usually False for recruitment pulses)

    Returns
    -------
    StateForcing
        Forcing object ready to use

    Examples
    --------
    >>> # Strong recruitment in 2005, weak in 2010
    >>> forcing = create_recruitment_forcing(
    ...     group_idx=3,
    ...     recruitment_multiplier={2005: 3.0, 2010: 0.5}
    ... )
    """
    forcing = StateForcing()
    forcing.add_forcing(
        group_idx=group_idx,
        variable=StateVariable.RECRUITMENT,
        time_series=recruitment_multiplier,
        years=years,
        mode=ForcingMode.MULTIPLY,
        interpolate=interpolate,
    )
    return forcing

    class BevertonHoltRecruitment(RecruitmentModel):
    """Beverton-Holt model: ``R = (alpha * SSB) / (1 + beta * SSB)``."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        alpha: float,
        beta: float,
        rmax: float = 1.0,
        name: str = "BevertonHolt",
    ):
        super().__init__(name=name, rmax=rmax)
        if alpha <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"alpha must be > 0, got {alpha}")
        if beta <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"beta must be > 0, got {beta}")
        self.alpha = float(alpha)
        self.beta = float(beta)

    def get_recruitment(
        self, ssb: float, time: float = 0.0, env_factor: float = 1.0
    ) -> float:
        _ = time
        ssb_val = self._sanitize_ssb(ssb)
        env = self._sanitize_env_factor(env_factor)
        base = (self.alpha * ssb_val) / (1.0 + self.beta * ssb_val)
        scaled = min(self.rmax, base) * env
        return max(0.01, float(scaled))

    def get_recruitment_batch(
        self,
        ssb_array: np.ndarray,
        time_array: np.ndarray,
        env_factors: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        ssb, _times, env = self._validate_array_lengths(
            ssb_array, time_array, env_factors
        )
        base = (self.alpha * ssb) / (1.0 + self.beta * ssb)
        scaled = np.minimum(self.rmax, base) * env
        return np.maximum(0.01, scaled)

    class LarvalConnectivity:
    """Larval dispersal model linking source and sink recruitment pools.

    Parameters
    ----------
    connectivity_matrix : np.ndarray
        Matrix with shape (n_targets, n_sources). Each column describes how
        recruits from one source distribute across target groups.
    source_groups : list[str]
        Source group names aligned to matrix columns.
    target_groups : list[str]
        Target group names aligned to matrix rows.
    survival_rate : float, optional
        Global larval survival applied after dispersal.
    normalize_columns : bool, optional
        If True, each source column is normalized to sum to 1 when positive.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        connectivity_matrix: np.ndarray,
        source_groups: list[str],
        target_groups: list[str],
        survival_rate: float = 1.0,
        normalize_columns: bool = True,
    ):
        matrix = np.asarray(connectivity_matrix, dtype=float)
        if matrix.ndim != 2:
            raise ValueError("connectivity_matrix must be 2D")
        if len(source_groups) != matrix.shape[1]:
            raise ValueError(
                "source_groups length must match connectivity_matrix columns"
            )
        if len(target_groups) != matrix.shape[0]:
            raise ValueError("target_groups length must match connectivity_matrix rows")
        if np.any(matrix < 0):
            raise ValueError("connectivity_matrix cannot contain negative values")

        self.source_groups = list(source_groups)
        self.target_groups = list(target_groups)
        self.connectivity_matrix = matrix.copy()
        if normalize_columns:
            col_sums = self.connectivity_matrix.sum(axis=0)
            positive = col_sums > 0
            self.connectivity_matrix[:, positive] = (
                self.connectivity_matrix[:, positive] / col_sums[positive]
            )

        self.set_survival_rate(survival_rate)

    def set_survival_rate(self, survival_rate: float) -> None:
        """Update larval survival rate."""
        survival = float(survival_rate)
        if survival < 0:
            raise ValueError("survival_rate must be >= 0")
        self.survival_rate = survival

    def get_connectivity(self, source_group: str, target_group: str) -> float:
        """Get dispersal proportion from source to target."""
        if source_group not in self.source_groups:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown source_group: {source_group}")
        if target_group not in self.target_groups:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown target_group: {target_group}")
        source_idx = self.source_groups.index(source_group)
        target_idx = self.target_groups.index(target_group)
        return float(self.connectivity_matrix[target_idx, source_idx])

    def apply_to_array(self, source_recruits: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """Apply connectivity to source recruitment vector."""
        recruits = np.asarray(source_recruits, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
        if recruits.size != len(self.source_groups):
            raise ValueError(
                "source_recruits length must match number of source_groups"
            )
        recruits = np.where(np.isfinite(recruits), np.maximum(0.0, recruits), 0.0)
        dispersed = self.connectivity_matrix @ recruits
        return dispersed * self.survival_rate

    def disperse(self, source_recruitment: dict[str, float]) -> dict[str, float]:
        """Disperse recruitment dictionary into target-group recruitment."""
        source_array = np.array(
            [float(source_recruitment.get(g, 0.0)) for g in self.source_groups],
            dtype=float,
        )
        target_array = self.apply_to_array(source_array)
        return {
            group: float(target_array[idx])
            for idx, group in enumerate(self.target_groups)
        }

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return (
            "LarvalConnectivity("
            f"sources={len(self.source_groups)}, targets={len(self.target_groups)}, "
            f"survival_rate={self.survival_rate})"
        )

    class MyersRecruitment(RecruitmentModel):
    """Myers-style saturating model: ``R = rmax * SSB^p / (k^p + SSB^p)``."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        rmax: float,
        k: float,
        power: float = 1.0,
        name: str = "Myers",
    ):
        super().__init__(name=name, rmax=rmax)
        if k <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"k must be > 0, got {k}")
        if power <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"power must be > 0, got {power}")
        self.k = float(k)
        self.power = float(power)

    def get_recruitment(
        self, ssb: float, time: float = 0.0, env_factor: float = 1.0
    ) -> float:
        _ = time
        ssb_val = self._sanitize_ssb(ssb)
        env = self._sanitize_env_factor(env_factor)
        ssb_pow = ssb_val**self.power
        k_pow = self.k**self.power
        base = self.rmax * ssb_pow / (k_pow + ssb_pow)
        scaled = base * env
        return max(0.01, float(scaled))

    def get_recruitment_batch(
        self,
        ssb_array: np.ndarray,
        time_array: np.ndarray,
        env_factors: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        ssb, _times, env = self._validate_array_lengths(
            ssb_array, time_array, env_factors
        )
        ssb_pow = ssb**self.power
        k_pow = self.k**self.power
        base = self.rmax * ssb_pow / (k_pow + ssb_pow)
        scaled = base * env
        return np.maximum(0.01, scaled)

    class RecruitmentModel(ABC):
    """Abstract base class for recruitment models.

    Recruitment models return multiplicative factors that can be applied to
    baseline recruitment. A factor of 1.0 indicates baseline recruitment.
    """

    def __init__(self, name: str = "RecruitmentModel", rmax: float = 1.0):
        """Initialize recruitment model.

        Parameters
        ----------
        name : str
            Human-readable model name.
        rmax : float
            Maximum scaling multiplier used by the model.
        """
        if rmax <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"rmax must be > 0, got {rmax}")
        self.name = name
        self.rmax = float(rmax)

    @abstractmethod
    def get_recruitment(
        self, ssb: float, time: float = 0.0, env_factor: float = 1.0
    ) -> float:
        """Get recruitment multiplier for one state."""
        raise NotImplementedError

    @abstractmethod
    def get_recruitment_batch(
        self,
        ssb_array: np.ndarray,
        time_array: np.ndarray,
        env_factors: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        """Get recruitment multipliers for arrays of states."""
        raise NotImplementedError

    def get_recruitment_trajectory(
        self, ssb_timeline: dict[float, float], times: np.ndarray
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        """Interpolate SSB across time and evaluate recruitment trajectory."""
        if not ssb_timeline:
            raise ValueError("ssb_timeline cannot be empty")

        times_arr = np.asarray(times, dtype=float)
        if times_arr.size == 0:
            raise ValueError("times cannot be empty")

        source_times = np.array(sorted(ssb_timeline.keys()), dtype=float)
        source_ssb = np.array([ssb_timeline[t] for t in source_times], dtype=float)

        if source_times.size == 1:
            ssb_values = np.full_like(times_arr, source_ssb[0], dtype=float)
        else:
            interp = interp1d(
                source_times,
                source_ssb,
                kind="linear",
                bounds_error=False,
                fill_value=(source_ssb[0], source_ssb[-1]),
            )
            ssb_values = np.asarray(interp(times_arr), dtype=float)

        return self.get_recruitment_batch(ssb_values, times_arr)

    @staticmethod
    def _sanitize_ssb(ssb: float) -> float:
        """Clamp invalid SSB values to a safe non-negative value."""
        if not np.isfinite(ssb):
            return 0.0
        return max(0.0, float(ssb))

    @staticmethod
    def _sanitize_env_factor(env_factor: float) -> float:
        """Use positive finite environmental factor or baseline fallback."""
        if not np.isfinite(env_factor) or env_factor <= 0:
            return 1.0
        return float(env_factor)

    @staticmethod
    def _validate_array_lengths(
        ssb_array: np.ndarray,
        time_array: np.ndarray,
        env_factors: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        """Validate and align vectorized recruitment inputs."""
        ssb = np.asarray(ssb_array, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
        times = np.asarray(time_array, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
        if ssb.size != times.size:
            raise ValueError(
                f"ssb_array (len {ssb.size}) and time_array (len {times.size}) "
                "must have same length"
            )

        if env_factors is None:
            env = np.ones_like(ssb, dtype=float)
        else:
            env = np.asarray(env_factors, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
            if env.size != ssb.size:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"env_factors (len {env.size}) must match ssb_array "
                    f"(len {ssb.size})"
                )

        ssb = np.where(np.isfinite(ssb), np.maximum(0.0, ssb), 0.0)
        env = np.where(np.isfinite(env) & (env > 0.0), env, 1.0)
        return ssb, times, env

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.__class__.__name__}(name={self.name!r}, rmax={self.rmax})"

    class RickerRecruitment(RecruitmentModel):
    """Ricker model: ``R = alpha * SSB * exp(-beta * SSB)``."""

    def __init__(
        self, alpha: float, beta: float, rmax: float = 1.0, name: str = "Ricker"
    ):
        super().__init__(name=name, rmax=rmax)
        if alpha <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"alpha must be > 0, got {alpha}")
        if beta <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"beta must be > 0, got {beta}")
        self.alpha = float(alpha)
        self.beta = float(beta)

    def get_recruitment(
        self, ssb: float, time: float = 0.0, env_factor: float = 1.0
    ) -> float:
        _ = time
        ssb_val = self._sanitize_ssb(ssb)
        env = self._sanitize_env_factor(env_factor)
        base = self.alpha * ssb_val * np.exp(-self.beta * ssb_val)
        scaled = min(self.rmax, base) * env
        return max(0.01, float(scaled))

    def get_recruitment_batch(
        self,
        ssb_array: np.ndarray,
        time_array: np.ndarray,
        env_factors: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        ssb, _times, env = self._validate_array_lengths(
            ssb_array, time_array, env_factors
        )
        base = self.alpha * ssb * np.exp(-self.beta * ssb)
        scaled = np.minimum(self.rmax, base) * env
        return np.maximum(0.01, scaled)

    def normalize_ssb_effect(
    ssb: float | np.ndarray, reference_ssb: float, effect_magnitude: float = 1.0
) -> float | np.ndarray:
    """Normalize SSB relative to a reference stock biomass."""
    if reference_ssb <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"reference_ssb must be > 0, got {reference_ssb}")

    ssb_values = np.asarray(ssb, dtype=float)
    safe_ssb = np.where(np.isfinite(ssb_values), np.maximum(0.0, ssb_values), 0.0)
    normalized = np.power(safe_ssb / reference_ssb, effect_magnitude)
    clipped = np.maximum(0.01, normalized)
    if np.isscalar(ssb):
        return float(clipped)
    return clipped

    def validate_recruitment_params(model_type: str, **kwargs) -> dict[str, float | str]:
    """Validate model parameters for recruitment model construction."""
    normalized = model_type.lower().replace("-", "").replace("_", "")
    if normalized == "ricker":
        required = {"alpha", "beta"}
        missing = required - set(kwargs)
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(f"Ricker requires {missing}, got {set(kwargs)}")
        alpha = float(kwargs["alpha"])
        beta = float(kwargs["beta"])
        if alpha <= 0 or beta <= 0:
            raise ValueError("Ricker alpha and beta must be > 0")
        allowed = {"alpha", "beta", "rmax", "name"}
    elif normalized == "bevertonholt":
        required = {"alpha", "beta"}
        missing = required - set(kwargs)
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(f"BevertonHolt requires {missing}, got {set(kwargs)}")
        alpha = float(kwargs["alpha"])
        beta = float(kwargs["beta"])
        if alpha <= 0 or beta <= 0:
            raise ValueError("BevertonHolt alpha and beta must be > 0")
        allowed = {"alpha", "beta", "rmax", "name"}
    elif normalized == "myers":
        required = {"rmax", "k"}
        missing = required - set(kwargs)
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(f"Myers requires {missing}, got {set(kwargs)}")
        rmax = float(kwargs["rmax"])
        k = float(kwargs["k"])
        if rmax <= 0 or k <= 0:
            raise ValueError("Myers rmax and k must be > 0")
        allowed = {"rmax", "k", "power", "name"}
    else:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown recruitment model_type '{model_type}'. Must be "
            "'Ricker', 'BevertonHolt', or 'Myers'."
        )
    return {k: v for k, v in kwargs.items() if k in allowed}

    def add_recruitment_support() -> None:
    """Monkey-patch RsimScenario with recruitment methods."""
    if hasattr(RsimScenario, "set_recruitment_model"):
        return

    def _init_recruitment(self: RsimScenario) -> None:
        if not hasattr(self, "_recruitment_models"):
            self._recruitment_models: Dict[str, RecruitmentModel] = {}
        if not hasattr(self, "_larval_connectivity"):
            self._larval_connectivity: Optional[LarvalConnectivity] = None

    def set_recruitment_model(
        self: RsimScenario, group_name: str, model: RecruitmentModel
    ) -> None:
        from pypath.core.recruitment import RecruitmentModel

        _init_recruitment(self)
        if group_name not in self.params.spname:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown group: {group_name}")
        if not isinstance(model, RecruitmentModel):
            raise TypeError(
                "model must be an instance of RecruitmentModel, "
                f"got {type(model).__name__}"
            )
        self._recruitment_models[group_name] = model

    def get_recruitment_model(
        self: RsimScenario, group_name: str
    ) -> Optional[RecruitmentModel]:
        _init_recruitment(self)
        return self._recruitment_models.get(group_name)

    def list_recruitment_models(self: RsimScenario) -> List[str]:
        _init_recruitment(self)
        return sorted(self._recruitment_models.keys())

    def set_larval_connectivity(
        self: RsimScenario, connectivity: Optional[LarvalConnectivity]
    ) -> None:
        from pypath.core.recruitment import LarvalConnectivity

        _init_recruitment(self)
        if connectivity is not None and not isinstance(
            connectivity, LarvalConnectivity
        ):
            raise TypeError(
                "connectivity must be LarvalConnectivity or None, "
                f"got {type(connectivity).__name__}"
            )
        self._larval_connectivity = connectivity

    def apply_recruitment(
        self: RsimScenario,
        time: float,
        ssb_by_group: Dict[str, float],
        env_factors: Optional[Dict[str, float]] = None,
    ) -> Dict[str, float]:
        _init_recruitment(self)

        time_val = float(time)
        outputs: Dict[str, float] = {}
        for group in self.params.spname:
            if group not in self._recruitment_models:
                outputs[group] = 1.0
                continue
            model = self._recruitment_models[group]
            ssb = float(ssb_by_group.get(group, 0.0))
            env = 1.0 if env_factors is None else float(env_factors.get(group, 1.0))
            outputs[group] = float(
                model.get_recruitment(ssb=ssb, time=time_val, env_factor=env)
            )

        if self._larval_connectivity is not None:
            dispersed = self._larval_connectivity.disperse(outputs)
            outputs.update(dispersed)

        return outputs

    def build_recruitment_vector(
        self: RsimScenario,
        time: float,
        ssb_by_group: Dict[str, float],
        env_factors: Optional[Dict[str, float]] = None,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        """Build (NUM_GROUPS+1)-length recruitment multiplier vector."""
        outputs = apply_recruitment(self, time, ssb_by_group, env_factors)
        vector = np.ones(self.params.NUM_GROUPS + 1, dtype=float)
        for idx, group in enumerate(self.params.spname):
            if idx >= vector.size:
                break
            vector[idx] = float(outputs.get(group, 1.0))
        return vector

    def apply_recruitment_to_forcing(
        self: RsimScenario,
        month_index: int,
        time: float,
        ssb_by_group: Dict[str, float],
        env_factors: Optional[Dict[str, float]] = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Write recruitment multipliers into scenario.forcing.ForcedRecs."""
        _init_recruitment(self)
        if (
            not hasattr(self, "forcing")
            or getattr(self.forcing, "ForcedRecs", None) is None
        ):
            raise ValueError("Scenario forcing.ForcedRecs is not available")
        if month_index < 0 or month_index >= self.forcing.ForcedRecs.shape[0]:
            raise ValueError(f"month_index out of bounds: {month_index}")

        self.forcing.ForcedRecs[month_index, :] = build_recruitment_vector(
            self,
            time=time,
            ssb_by_group=ssb_by_group,
            env_factors=env_factors,
        )

    def get_recruitment_trajectory(
        self: RsimScenario,
        group_name: str,
        ssb_timeline: Dict[float, float],
        times: np.ndarray,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        _init_recruitment(self)
        model = self._recruitment_models.get(group_name)
        if model is None:
            raise ValueError(f"No recruitment model registered for group: {group_name}")
        return model.get_recruitment_trajectory(
            ssb_timeline=ssb_timeline, times=np.asarray(times)
        )

    def batch_recruitment_evaluation(
        self: RsimScenario,
        groups: List[str],
        ssb_matrix: np.ndarray,
        time_array: np.ndarray,
        env_matrix: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
    ) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
        _init_recruitment(self)

        ssb = np.asarray(ssb_matrix, dtype=float)
        times = np.asarray(time_array, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
        if ssb.ndim != 2:
            raise ValueError("ssb_matrix must be a 2D array")
        if ssb.shape[0] != len(groups):
            raise ValueError("ssb_matrix row count must match number of groups")
        if ssb.shape[1] != len(times):
            raise ValueError("ssb_matrix column count must match time_array length")

        if env_matrix is not None:
            env = np.asarray(env_matrix, dtype=float)
            if env.shape != ssb.shape:
                raise ValueError("env_matrix must have same shape as ssb_matrix")
        else:
            env = None

        result: Dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
        for i, group in enumerate(groups):
            model = self._recruitment_models.get(group)
            if model is None:
                result[group] = np.ones(len(times), dtype=float)
                continue

            group_env = None if env is None else env[i, :]
            result[group] = model.get_recruitment_batch(
                ssb_array=ssb[i, :],
                time_array=times,
                env_factors=group_env,
            )
        return result

    RsimScenario._init_recruitment = _init_recruitment
    RsimScenario.set_recruitment_model = set_recruitment_model
    RsimScenario.get_recruitment_model = get_recruitment_model
    RsimScenario.list_recruitment_models = list_recruitment_models
    RsimScenario.set_larval_connectivity = set_larval_connectivity
    RsimScenario.apply_recruitment = apply_recruitment
    RsimScenario.build_recruitment_vector = build_recruitment_vector
    RsimScenario.apply_recruitment_to_forcing = apply_recruitment_to_forcing
    RsimScenario.get_recruitment_trajectory = get_recruitment_trajectory
    RsimScenario.batch_recruitment_evaluation = batch_recruitment_evaluation

    @dataclass(frozen=True)
class MetabolicModel:
    """Metabolic scaling model with allometric and thermal dependence.

    Parameters
    ----------
    base_metabolism : float
        Baseline metabolic rate at reference mass and temperature.
    mass_exponent : float
        Allometric exponent for body-mass scaling.
    reference_mass : float
        Body mass where mass-scaling multiplier equals 1.0.
    temperature_dependence : TemperatureDependence, optional
        Temperature model (defaults to q10=2.0 at 10°C).
    activity_budget : float
        Baseline activity multiplier.
    """

    base_metabolism: float
    mass_exponent: float = 0.75
    reference_mass: float = 1.0
    temperature_dependence: Optional[TemperatureDependence] = None
    activity_budget: float = 1.0

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.base_metabolism <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"base_metabolism must be > 0, got {self.base_metabolism}")
        if self.reference_mass <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"reference_mass must be > 0, got {self.reference_mass}")
        if self.activity_budget <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"activity_budget must be > 0, got {self.activity_budget}")
        if self.temperature_dependence is None:
            object.__setattr__(
                self,
                "temperature_dependence",
                TemperatureDependence(),
            )

    def compute_mass_factor(self, body_mass: float | np.ndarray) -> float | np.ndarray:
        """Compute allometric mass scaling factor."""
        mass_arr = np.asarray(body_mass, dtype=float)
        mass_safe = np.where(np.isfinite(mass_arr), np.maximum(mass_arr, 0.0), 0.0)
        ratio = np.where(
            mass_safe > 0.0,
            mass_safe / self.reference_mass,
            0.0,
        )
        factor = np.power(ratio, self.mass_exponent)
        if np.isscalar(body_mass):
            return float(factor)
        return factor

    def compute_temperature_factor(
        self, temperature: float | np.ndarray
    ) -> float | np.ndarray:
        """Compute thermal scaling factor using configured Q10 model."""
        return self.temperature_dependence.compute_q10_factor(temperature)

    def compute_metabolic_rate(
        self,
        body_mass: float,
        temperature: float,
        activity_multiplier: float = 1.0,
    ) -> float:
        """Compute metabolic rate for a single body mass and temperature."""
        if activity_multiplier <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"activity_multiplier must be > 0, got {activity_multiplier}"
            )
        mass_factor = self.compute_mass_factor(body_mass)
        temp_factor = self.compute_temperature_factor(temperature)
        return float(
            self.base_metabolism
            * mass_factor
            * temp_factor
            * self.activity_budget
            * activity_multiplier
        )

    def compute_metabolic_rate_batch(
        self,
        body_mass: np.ndarray,
        temperature: np.ndarray,
        activity_multiplier: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        """Compute metabolic rates for vector inputs."""
        mass_arr = np.asarray(body_mass, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
        temp_arr = np.asarray(temperature, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
        if mass_arr.size != temp_arr.size:
            raise ValueError(
                f"body_mass length ({mass_arr.size}) must equal "
                f"temperature length ({temp_arr.size})"
            )

        if activity_multiplier is None:
            activity = np.ones_like(mass_arr)
        else:
            activity = np.asarray(activity_multiplier, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
            if activity.size != mass_arr.size:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"activity_multiplier length ({activity.size}) must equal "
                    f"body_mass length ({mass_arr.size})"
                )
            if np.any(activity <= 0):
                raise ValueError("activity_multiplier values must all be > 0")

        mass_factor = np.asarray(self.compute_mass_factor(mass_arr), dtype=float)
        temp_factor = np.asarray(self.compute_temperature_factor(temp_arr), dtype=float)

        return (
            self.base_metabolism
            * mass_factor
            * temp_factor
            * self.activity_budget
            * activity
        )

    @dataclass(frozen=True)
class TemperatureDependence:
    """Q10-based temperature dependence model.

    Parameters
    ----------
    q10_coefficient : float
        Multiplicative increase in rate per +10°C.
    reference_temperature : float
        Reference temperature where factor equals 1.0.
    min_factor : float, optional
        Lower clamp for computed factors.
    max_factor : float, optional
        Upper clamp for computed factors.
    """

    q10_coefficient: float = 2.0
    reference_temperature: float = 10.0
    min_factor: float = 0.01
    max_factor: float = 100.0

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.q10_coefficient <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"q10_coefficient must be > 0, got {self.q10_coefficient}")
        if self.min_factor <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"min_factor must be > 0, got {self.min_factor}")
        if self.max_factor < self.min_factor:
            raise ValueError(
                f"max_factor ({self.max_factor}) must be >= min_factor ({self.min_factor})"
            )

    def compute_q10_factor(self, temperature: float | np.ndarray) -> float | np.ndarray:
        """Compute temperature scaling factor using the Q10 formulation."""
        temp_arr = np.asarray(temperature, dtype=float)
        factor = self.q10_coefficient ** (
            (temp_arr - self.reference_temperature) / 10.0
        )
        factor = np.clip(factor, self.min_factor, self.max_factor)
        if np.isscalar(temperature):
            return float(factor)
        return factor

    def compute_q10_factor(self, temperature: float | np.ndarray) -> float | np.ndarray:
    """Compute temperature scaling factor using the Q10 formulation."""
    temp_arr = np.asarray(temperature, dtype=float)
    factor = self.q10_coefficient ** (
        (temp_arr - self.reference_temperature) / 10.0
    )
    factor = np.clip(factor, self.min_factor, self.max_factor)
    if np.isscalar(temperature):
        return float(factor)
    return factor

    def apply_size_dependent_rates(
    base_rates: np.ndarray,
    body_mass: np.ndarray,
    mass_exponent: float,
    reference_mass: float = 1.0,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Apply allometric mass scaling to an array of baseline rates."""
    if reference_mass <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"reference_mass must be > 0, got {reference_mass}")
    rates = np.asarray(base_rates, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
    masses = np.asarray(body_mass, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
    if rates.size != masses.size:
        raise ValueError(
            f"base_rates length ({rates.size}) must equal body_mass length ({masses.size})"
        )

    masses = np.where(np.isfinite(masses), np.maximum(masses, 0.0), 0.0)
    factors = np.power(
        np.where(masses > 0.0, masses / reference_mass, 0.0), mass_exponent
    )
    return rates * factors

    def compute_temperature_adjusted_metabolism(
    base_metabolism: float | np.ndarray,
    temperature: float | np.ndarray,
    temperature_model: TemperatureDependence,
) -> float | np.ndarray:
    """Apply thermal scaling to baseline metabolism using a temperature model."""
    base = np.asarray(base_metabolism, dtype=float)
    factor = np.asarray(temperature_model.compute_q10_factor(temperature), dtype=float)
    adjusted = base * factor
    if np.isscalar(base_metabolism) and np.isscalar(temperature):
        return float(adjusted)
    return adjusted

    @dataclass
class DynamicLogisticSelectivity(SelectivityPattern):
    """Logistic selectivity with optional time-varying L50.

    S(L) = 1 / (1 + exp(-k * (L - L50_t))).
    """

    l50: float
    slope: float
    l50_time_series: Optional[Dict[float, float]] = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.slope <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"slope must be > 0, got {self.slope}")

    def _l50_at(self, time: Optional[float]) -> float:
        if not self.l50_time_series or time is None:
            return float(self.l50)
        xs = np.array(sorted(self.l50_time_series.keys()), dtype=float)
        ys = np.array([self.l50_time_series[x] for x in xs], dtype=float)
        if xs.size == 1:
            return float(ys[0])
        return float(np.interp(float(time), xs, ys, left=ys[0], right=ys[-1]))

    def evaluate(
        self,
        lengths: np.ndarray,
        time: Optional[float] = None,
        space: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        _ = space
        L = np.asarray(lengths, dtype=float)
        l50_t = self._l50_at(time)
        sel = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-self.slope * (L - l50_t)))
        return np.clip(sel, 0.0, 1.0)

    @dataclass
class FishingOptimization:
    """Simple fishing optimization utility functions."""

    min_effort: float = 0.0
    max_effort: float = 10.0

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.max_effort < self.min_effort:
            raise ValueError("max_effort must be >= min_effort")

    def constrain_sustainability(
        self,
        effort: np.ndarray,
        biomass: np.ndarray,
        biomass_threshold: float,
        reduction_factor: float = 0.5,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        """Reduce effort where biomass is below threshold."""
        eff = np.asarray(effort, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
        bio = np.asarray(biomass, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
        if eff.size != bio.size:
            raise ValueError("effort and biomass must have same length")
        if reduction_factor < 0 or reduction_factor > 1:
            raise ValueError("reduction_factor must be in [0, 1]")

        out = eff.copy()
        out[bio < biomass_threshold] *= reduction_factor
        return np.clip(out, self.min_effort, self.max_effort)

    def maximize_revenue(
        self,
        catchability: np.ndarray,
        biomass: np.ndarray,
        price: np.ndarray,
        effort_budget: float,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        """Allocate effort proportional to marginal revenue potential."""
        q = np.asarray(catchability, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
        b = np.asarray(biomass, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
        p = np.asarray(price, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
        if not (q.size == b.size == p.size):
            raise ValueError("catchability, biomass, and price must have same length")
        if effort_budget < 0:
            raise ValueError("effort_budget must be >= 0")

        scores = np.maximum(0.0, q * b * p)
        if np.all(scores == 0):
            return np.zeros_like(scores)

        alloc = effort_budget * scores / np.sum(scores)
        return np.clip(alloc, self.min_effort, self.max_effort)

    def minimize_bycatch(
        self,
        effort: np.ndarray,
        bycatch_risk: np.ndarray,
        target_reduction: float,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        """Reduce effort in high-bycatch-risk fleets first."""
        eff = np.asarray(effort, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
        risk = np.asarray(bycatch_risk, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
        if eff.size != risk.size:
            raise ValueError("effort and bycatch_risk must have same length")
        if target_reduction < 0:
            raise ValueError("target_reduction must be >= 0")

        remaining = target_reduction
        out = eff.copy()
        order = np.argsort(-risk)  # high risk first
        for idx in order:
            if remaining <= 0:
                break
            reducible = min(out[idx], remaining)
            out[idx] -= reducible
            remaining -= reducible

        return np.clip(out, self.min_effort, self.max_effort)

    @dataclass
class SpatialSelectivity(SelectivityPattern):
    """Spatially varying selectivity using per-zone multipliers."""

    base_pattern: np.ndarray
    zone_multipliers: Dict[str, float]

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        base = np.asarray(self.base_pattern, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
        if base.size == 0:
            raise ValueError("base_pattern cannot be empty")
        self.base_pattern = base

    def evaluate(
        self,
        lengths: np.ndarray,
        time: Optional[float] = None,
        space: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        _ = time
        L = np.asarray(lengths, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
        if L.size != self.base_pattern.size:
            raise ValueError(
                f"lengths size ({L.size}) must match base_pattern size ({self.base_pattern.size})"
            )
        mult = 1.0 if space is None else float(self.zone_multipliers.get(space, 1.0))
        out = self.base_pattern * mult
        return np.clip(out, 0.0, 1.0)

    @dataclass
class TimeVaryingSelectivity(SelectivityPattern):
    """Time-varying multiplicative selectivity profile."""

    base_pattern: np.ndarray
    time_multipliers: Dict[float, float]

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        base = np.asarray(self.base_pattern, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
        if base.size == 0:
            raise ValueError("base_pattern cannot be empty")
        if np.any(base < 0):
            raise ValueError("base_pattern values must be >= 0")
        self.base_pattern = base

    def _time_multiplier(self, time: Optional[float]) -> float:
        if time is None or not self.time_multipliers:
            return 1.0
        xs = np.array(sorted(self.time_multipliers.keys()), dtype=float)
        ys = np.array([self.time_multipliers[x] for x in xs], dtype=float)
        if xs.size == 1:
            return float(ys[0])
        return float(np.interp(float(time), xs, ys, left=ys[0], right=ys[-1]))

    def evaluate(
        self,
        lengths: np.ndarray,
        time: Optional[float] = None,
        space: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        _ = space
        L = np.asarray(lengths, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
        if L.size != self.base_pattern.size:
            raise ValueError(
                f"lengths size ({L.size}) must match base_pattern size ({self.base_pattern.size})"
            )
        out = self.base_pattern * self._time_multiplier(time)
        return np.clip(out, 0.0, 1.0)

    @dataclass
class RiskAssessment:
    """Risk metrics for extinction/collapse under uncertainty."""

    def compute_extinction_risk(self, biomass: ArrayLike, threshold: float) -> float:
        """Probability biomass falls below extinction threshold."""
        b = np.asarray(biomass, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
        if b.size == 0:
            raise ValueError("biomass cannot be empty")
        return float(np.mean(b < threshold))

    def compute_collapse_risk(
        self,
        biomass: ArrayLike,
        baseline_biomass: float,
        collapse_fraction: float = 0.2,
    ) -> float:
        """Probability biomass falls below collapse fraction of baseline."""
        if baseline_biomass <= 0:
            raise ValueError("baseline_biomass must be > 0")
        if not (0 < collapse_fraction < 1):
            raise ValueError("collapse_fraction must be in (0, 1)")
        threshold = baseline_biomass * collapse_fraction
        return self.compute_extinction_risk(biomass, threshold)

    def worst_case_analysis(self, outputs: ArrayLike) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """Summarize worst-case, best-case, and spread."""
        y = np.asarray(outputs, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
        if y.size == 0:
            raise ValueError("outputs cannot be empty")
        return {
            "min": float(np.min(y)),
            "max": float(np.max(y)),
            "range": float(np.max(y) - np.min(y)),
            "mean": float(np.mean(y)),
        }

    @dataclass
class SensitivityAnalyzer:
    """Compute local/global sensitivity diagnostics for model outputs."""

    step_fraction: float = 0.01

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.step_fraction <= 0:
            raise ValueError("step_fraction must be > 0")

    def compute_local_sensitivity(
        self,
        model_func: ModelFunc,
        baseline_params: ArrayLike,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        """Finite-difference local sensitivity around baseline parameters."""
        x0 = np.asarray(baseline_params, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
        base = float(model_func(x0))
        out = np.zeros_like(x0)

        for i in range(x0.size):
            step = self.step_fraction * max(abs(x0[i]), 1.0)
            xp = x0.copy()
            xm = x0.copy()
            xp[i] += step
            xm[i] -= step
            fp = float(model_func(xp))
            fm = float(model_func(xm))
            derivative = (fp - fm) / (2.0 * step)
            out[i] = derivative * (x0[i] / base) if base != 0 else derivative
        return out

    def compute_global_sensitivity(
        self,
        samples: np.ndarray,
        outputs: np.ndarray,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        """Approximate global sensitivity via absolute Pearson correlation."""
        X = np.asarray(samples, dtype=float)
        y = np.asarray(outputs, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
        if X.ndim != 2:
            raise ValueError("samples must be 2D")
        if X.shape[0] != y.size:
            raise ValueError("samples rows must equal outputs length")

        sens = np.zeros(X.shape[1], dtype=float)
        for j in range(X.shape[1]):
            xj = X[:, j]
            if np.std(xj) == 0 or np.std(y) == 0:
                sens[j] = 0.0
            else:
                sens[j] = abs(float(np.corrcoef(xj, y)[0, 1]))
        total = np.sum(sens)
        return sens / total if total > 0 else sens

    def morris_screening(
        self,
        model_func: ModelFunc,
        bounds: np.ndarray,
        n_trajectories: int = 20,
        delta: float = 0.1,
        random_seed: int | None = None,
    ) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
        """Compute Morris elementary effects summary statistics."""
        b = np.asarray(bounds, dtype=float)
        if b.ndim != 2 or b.shape[1] != 2:
            raise ValueError("bounds must have shape (n_params, 2)")
        if n_trajectories <= 0:
            raise ValueError("n_trajectories must be > 0")
        if not (0 < delta < 1):
            raise ValueError("delta must be in (0, 1)")

        rng = np.random.default_rng(random_seed)
        n_params = b.shape[0]
        effects = [[] for _ in range(n_params)]

        for _ in range(n_trajectories):
            x = rng.uniform(b[:, 0], b[:, 1])
            f0 = float(model_func(x))
            for j in range(n_params):
                span = b[j, 1] - b[j, 0]
                step = delta * span
                if step == 0:
                    effects[j].append(0.0)
                    continue
                xj = x.copy()
                xj[j] = np.clip(xj[j] + step, b[j, 0], b[j, 1])
                fj = float(model_func(xj))
                ee = (fj - f0) / step
                effects[j].append(ee)

        ee_array = np.array([np.array(v) for v in effects], dtype=float)
        mu_star = np.mean(np.abs(ee_array), axis=1)
        sigma = np.std(ee_array, axis=1, ddof=0)
        return {"mu_star": mu_star, "sigma": sigma, "effects": ee_array}

    def compute_global_sensitivity(
    self,
    samples: np.ndarray,
    outputs: np.ndarray,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Approximate global sensitivity via absolute Pearson correlation."""
    X = np.asarray(samples, dtype=float)
    y = np.asarray(outputs, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
    if X.ndim != 2:
        raise ValueError("samples must be 2D")
    if X.shape[0] != y.size:
        raise ValueError("samples rows must equal outputs length")

    sens = np.zeros(X.shape[1], dtype=float)
    for j in range(X.shape[1]):
        xj = X[:, j]
        if np.std(xj) == 0 or np.std(y) == 0:
            sens[j] = 0.0
        else:
            sens[j] = abs(float(np.corrcoef(xj, y)[0, 1]))
    total = np.sum(sens)
    return sens / total if total > 0 else sens

    def compute_local_sensitivity(
    self,
    model_func: ModelFunc,
    baseline_params: ArrayLike,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Finite-difference local sensitivity around baseline parameters."""
    x0 = np.asarray(baseline_params, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
    base = float(model_func(x0))
    out = np.zeros_like(x0)

    for i in range(x0.size):
        step = self.step_fraction * max(abs(x0[i]), 1.0)
        xp = x0.copy()
        xm = x0.copy()
        xp[i] += step
        xm[i] -= step
        fp = float(model_func(xp))
        fm = float(model_func(xm))
        derivative = (fp - fm) / (2.0 * step)
        out[i] = derivative * (x0[i] / base) if base != 0 else derivative
    return out

    def morris_screening(
    self,
    model_func: ModelFunc,
    bounds: np.ndarray,
    n_trajectories: int = 20,
    delta: float = 0.1,
    random_seed: int | None = None,
) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    """Compute Morris elementary effects summary statistics."""
    b = np.asarray(bounds, dtype=float)
    if b.ndim != 2 or b.shape[1] != 2:
        raise ValueError("bounds must have shape (n_params, 2)")
    if n_trajectories <= 0:
        raise ValueError("n_trajectories must be > 0")
    if not (0 < delta < 1):
        raise ValueError("delta must be in (0, 1)")

    rng = np.random.default_rng(random_seed)
    n_params = b.shape[0]
    effects = [[] for _ in range(n_params)]

    for _ in range(n_trajectories):
        x = rng.uniform(b[:, 0], b[:, 1])
        f0 = float(model_func(x))
        for j in range(n_params):
            span = b[j, 1] - b[j, 0]
            step = delta * span
            if step == 0:
                effects[j].append(0.0)
                continue
            xj = x.copy()
            xj[j] = np.clip(xj[j] + step, b[j, 0], b[j, 1])
            fj = float(model_func(xj))
            ee = (fj - f0) / step
            effects[j].append(ee)

    ee_array = np.array([np.array(v) for v in effects], dtype=float)
    mu_star = np.mean(np.abs(ee_array), axis=1)
    sigma = np.std(ee_array, axis=1, ddof=0)
    return {"mu_star": mu_star, "sigma": sigma, "effects": ee_array}

    @dataclass
class UncertaintyPropagation:
    """Monte Carlo and sampling helpers for output uncertainty."""

    def latin_hypercube_sampling(
        self,
        bounds: np.ndarray,
        n_samples: int,
        random_seed: int | None = None,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        """Generate Latin Hypercube samples for bounded parameters."""
        b = np.asarray(bounds, dtype=float)
        if b.ndim != 2 or b.shape[1] != 2:
            raise ValueError("bounds must have shape (n_params, 2)")
        if n_samples <= 0:
            raise ValueError("n_samples must be > 0")

        rng = np.random.default_rng(random_seed)
        n_params = b.shape[0]
        out = np.zeros((n_samples, n_params), dtype=float)

        for j in range(n_params):
            low, high = b[j]
            if high < low:
                raise ValueError("each bounds row must satisfy high >= low")
            cut = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, n_samples + 1)
            u = rng.uniform(cut[:-1], cut[1:])
            rng.shuffle(u)
            out[:, j] = low + u * (high - low)
        return out

    def monte_carlo_ensemble(
        self,
        model_func: ModelFunc,
        samples: np.ndarray,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        """Evaluate model outputs for sample matrix."""
        X = np.asarray(samples, dtype=float)
        if X.ndim != 2:
            raise ValueError("samples must be 2D")
        return np.array([float(model_func(row)) for row in X], dtype=float)

    def quantile_analysis(
        self,
        outputs: ArrayLike,
        quantiles: Iterable[float] = (0.05, 0.5, 0.95),
    ) -> Dict[float, float]:
        """Compute quantiles for an output distribution."""
        y = np.asarray(outputs, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
        if y.size == 0:
            raise ValueError("outputs cannot be empty")
        q = np.array(list(quantiles), dtype=float)
        if np.any((q < 0) | (q > 1)):
            raise ValueError("quantiles must be within [0, 1]")
        vals = np.quantile(y, q)
        return {float(qq): float(vv) for qq, vv in zip(q, vals)}

    class EcosimOptimizer:
    """Bayesian optimizer for Ecosim parameters.

    Calibrates Ecosim parameters to match observed biomass time series using
    Bayesian optimization with Gaussian Processes.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : Rpath
        Balanced Ecopath model
    params : RpathParams
        Model parameters
    observed_data : dict
        Dictionary mapping group indices to observed biomass time series
        Example: {1: np.array([1.0, 1.2, 1.1, ...]), 2: np.array([0.5, 0.6, ...])}
    years : range
        Years to simulate
    objective : str or callable
        Objective function to minimize. Options:
        - 'mse': Mean squared error
        - 'mape': Mean absolute percentage error
        - 'nrmse': Normalized root mean squared error
        - 'loglik': Negative log-likelihood
        - callable: Custom function(y_true, y_pred) -> float
    verbose : bool
        Print optimization progress

    Attributes
    ----------
    model : Rpath
        Ecopath model
    params : RpathParams
        Model parameters
    observed_data : dict
        Observed time series
    years : range
        Simulation years
    objective_func : callable
        Objective function
    verbose : bool
        Verbosity flag
    n_calls : int
        Number of function evaluations performed
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        model: Rpath,
        params: RpathParams,
        observed_data: Dict[int, np.ndarray],
        years: range,
        objective: str = "mse",
        verbose: bool = True,
    ):
        if not HAS_SKOPT:
            raise ImportError(
                "scikit-optimize is required for Bayesian optimization. "
                "Install with: pip install scikit-optimize"
            )

        self.model = model
        self.params = params
        self.observed_data = observed_data
        self.years = years
        self.verbose = verbose
        self.n_calls = 0

        # Set objective function
        if isinstance(objective, str):
            objective_funcs = {
                "mse": mean_squared_error,
                "mape": mean_absolute_percentage_error,
                "nrmse": normalized_root_mean_squared_error,
                "loglik": log_likelihood,
            }
            if objective not in objective_funcs:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Unknown objective: {objective}. Choose from {list(objective_funcs.keys())}"
                )
            self.objective_func = objective_funcs[objective]
        else:
            self.objective_func = objective

        # Validate observed data
        self._validate_observed_data()

    def _validate_observed_data(self) -> None:
        """Validate observed data format and dimensions."""
        n_years = len(self.years)
        for group_idx, data in self.observed_data.items():
            if len(data) != n_years:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Observed data for group {group_idx} has {len(data)} points "
                    f"but simulation has {n_years} years"
                )
            if group_idx < 1 or group_idx > self.model.NUM_LIVING:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Group index {group_idx} out of range [1, {self.model.NUM_LIVING}]"
                )

    def _run_simulation(self, param_dict: Dict[str, float]) -> np.ndarray:
        """Run Ecosim simulation with given parameters.

        Parameters
        ----------
        param_dict : dict
            Dictionary of parameter values

        Returns
        -------
        np.ndarray
            Simulated biomass for observed groups
        """
        # Create scenario with parameters
        scenario = rsim_scenario(self.model, self.params, years=self.years)

        # Update parameters
        for param_name, value in param_dict.items():
            self._update_scenario_parameter(scenario, param_name, value)

        # Run simulation
        try:
            result = rsim_run(scenario, method="RK4")

            # Extract biomass for observed groups
            simulated = {}
            for group_idx in self.observed_data.keys():
                # Annual biomass: shape (n_years, n_groups+1)
                # Group indices start at 1 (0 is "Outside")
                simulated[group_idx] = result.annual_Biomass[:, group_idx]

            return simulated
        except Exception as e:
            if self.verbose:
                logger.error(f"Simulation failed with parameters {param_dict}: {e}")
            # Return high penalty for failed simulations
            return None

    def _update_scenario_parameter(
        self, scenario: RsimScenario, param_name: str, value: float
    ) -> None:
        """Update a parameter in the scenario.

        Parameters
        ----------
        scenario : RsimScenario
            Simulation scenario
        param_name : str
            Parameter name (e.g., 'VV_1', 'QQ_5', 'vulnerability')
        value : float
            Parameter value
        """
        if param_name == "vulnerability":
            # Update base vulnerability for all groups
            scenario.params.VV[:] = value
        elif param_name.startswith("VV_"):
            # Update specific group vulnerability
            group_idx = int(param_name.split("_")[1])
            scenario.params.VV[group_idx] = value
        elif param_name.startswith("QQ_"):
            # Update specific link QQ
            link_idx = int(param_name.split("_")[1])
            scenario.params.QQ[link_idx] = value
        elif param_name.startswith("DD_"):
            # Update specific link DD
            link_idx = int(param_name.split("_")[1])
            scenario.params.DD[link_idx] = value
        elif param_name.startswith("PB_"):
            # Update specific group PB
            group_idx = int(param_name.split("_")[1])
            scenario.params.PBopt[group_idx] = value
        elif param_name.startswith("QB_"):
            # Update specific group QB
            group_idx = int(param_name.split("_")[1])
            scenario.params.QBopt[group_idx] = value
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown parameter: {param_name}")

    def _calculate_objective(self, simulated: Dict[int, np.ndarray]) -> float:
        """Calculate objective function value.

        Parameters
        ----------
        simulated : dict
            Simulated biomass for each group

        Returns
        -------
        float
            Objective function value (lower is better)
        """
        if simulated is None:
            return 1e10  # High penalty for failed simulations

        total_error = 0.0
        n_groups = len(self.observed_data)

        for group_idx, observed in self.observed_data.items():
            predicted = simulated[group_idx]
            error = self.objective_func(observed, predicted)
            total_error += error

        # Average across groups
        return total_error / n_groups

    def optimize(
        self,
        param_bounds: Dict[str, Tuple[float, float]],
        n_calls: int = 50,
        n_initial_points: int = 10,
        random_state: int = 42,
    ) -> OptimizationResult:
        """Run Bayesian optimization.

        Parameters
        ----------
        param_bounds : dict
            Dictionary mapping parameter names to (min, max) bounds
            Example: {'vulnerability': (1.0, 5.0), 'VV_3': (1.0, 10.0)}
        n_calls : int
            Number of function evaluations
        n_initial_points : int
            Number of random initial points before Bayesian optimization
        random_state : int
            Random seed for reproducibility

        Returns
        -------
        OptimizationResult
            Optimization results including best parameters and convergence
        """
        import time

        start_time = time.time()

        # Define search space
        dimensions = []
        param_names = []
        for name, (low, high) in param_bounds.items():
            dimensions.append(Real(low, high, name=name))
            param_names.append(name)

        # Store all evaluations
        all_params_list = []
        all_scores = []

        # Define objective function for skopt
        @use_named_args(dimensions)
        def objective(**params):
            self.n_calls += 1

            if self.verbose:
                logger.info(f"=== Iteration {self.n_calls}/{n_calls} ===")
                logger.info(
                    "Parameters: %s", {k: f"{v:.4f}" for k, v in params.items()}
                )

            # Run simulation
            simulated = self._run_simulation(params)

            # Calculate objective
            score = self._calculate_objective(simulated)

            if self.verbose:
                logger.info(f"Objective: {score:.6f}")

            # Store results
            all_params_list.append(params.copy())
            all_scores.append(score)

            return score

        # Run optimization
        if self.verbose:
            logger.info(f"Starting Bayesian optimization with {n_calls} evaluations...")
            logger.info(f"Optimizing parameters: {list(param_bounds.keys())}")
            logger.info(f"Observed groups: {list(self.observed_data.keys())}")
            logger.info(f"Simulation years: {len(self.years)}")

        self.n_calls = 0
        result = gp_minimize(
            objective,
            dimensions,
            n_calls=n_calls,
            n_initial_points=n_initial_points,
            random_state=random_state,
            verbose=False,
        )

        optimization_time = time.time() - start_time

        # Extract results
        best_params = {name: value for name, value in zip(param_names, result.x)}
        best_score = result.fun
        convergence = [np.min(all_scores[: i + 1]) for i in range(len(all_scores))]

        if self.verbose:
            logger.info(f"{'=' * 60}")
            logger.info("OPTIMIZATION COMPLETE")
            logger.info(f"{'=' * 60}")
            logger.info(f"Best score: {best_score:.6f}")
            logger.info("Best parameters:")
            for name, value in best_params.items():
                logger.info(f"  {name}: {value:.4f}")
            logger.info(f"Total evaluations: {self.n_calls}")
            logger.info(f"Optimization time: {optimization_time:.2f} seconds")
            logger.info(f"{'=' * 60}")

        return OptimizationResult(
            best_params=best_params,
            best_score=best_score,
            n_iterations=self.n_calls,
            convergence=convergence,
            all_params=all_params_list,
            all_scores=all_scores,
            optimization_time=optimization_time,
        )

    def validate(
        self,
        params: Dict[str, float],
        test_data: Optional[Dict[int, np.ndarray]] = None,
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Validate optimized parameters on test data.

        Parameters
        ----------
        params : dict
            Parameter values to validate
        test_data : dict, optional
            Test data. If None, uses training data (self.observed_data)

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            Validation metrics for each group and overall
        """
        if test_data is None:
            test_data = self.observed_data

        # Run simulation with optimized parameters
        simulated = self._run_simulation(params)

        if simulated is None:
            return {"error": "Simulation failed"}

        # Calculate metrics for each group
        results = {}
        for group_idx, observed in test_data.items():
            predicted = simulated[group_idx]

            results[f"group_{group_idx}"] = {
                "mse": mean_squared_error(observed, predicted),
                "mape": mean_absolute_percentage_error(observed, predicted),
                "nrmse": normalized_root_mean_squared_error(observed, predicted),
                "correlation": np.corrcoef(observed, predicted)[0, 1],
            }

        # Calculate overall metrics
        all_observed = np.concatenate([test_data[idx] for idx in test_data.keys()])
        all_predicted = np.concatenate([simulated[idx] for idx in test_data.keys()])

        results["overall"] = {
            "mse": mean_squared_error(all_observed, all_predicted),
            "mape": mean_absolute_percentage_error(all_observed, all_predicted),
            "nrmse": normalized_root_mean_squared_error(all_observed, all_predicted),
            "correlation": np.corrcoef(all_observed, all_predicted)[0, 1],
        }

        return results

    def optimize(
    self,
    param_bounds: Dict[str, Tuple[float, float]],
    n_calls: int = 50,
    n_initial_points: int = 10,
    random_state: int = 42,
) -> OptimizationResult:
    """Run Bayesian optimization.

    Parameters
    ----------
    param_bounds : dict
        Dictionary mapping parameter names to (min, max) bounds
        Example: {'vulnerability': (1.0, 5.0), 'VV_3': (1.0, 10.0)}
    n_calls : int
        Number of function evaluations
    n_initial_points : int
        Number of random initial points before Bayesian optimization
    random_state : int
        Random seed for reproducibility

    Returns
    -------
    OptimizationResult
        Optimization results including best parameters and convergence
    """
    import time

    start_time = time.time()

    # Define search space
    dimensions = []
    param_names = []
    for name, (low, high) in param_bounds.items():
        dimensions.append(Real(low, high, name=name))
        param_names.append(name)

    # Store all evaluations
    all_params_list = []
    all_scores = []

    # Define objective function for skopt
    @use_named_args(dimensions)
    def objective(**params):
        self.n_calls += 1

        if self.verbose:
            logger.info(f"=== Iteration {self.n_calls}/{n_calls} ===")
            logger.info(
                "Parameters: %s", {k: f"{v:.4f}" for k, v in params.items()}
            )

        # Run simulation
        simulated = self._run_simulation(params)

        # Calculate objective
        score = self._calculate_objective(simulated)

        if self.verbose:
            logger.info(f"Objective: {score:.6f}")

        # Store results
        all_params_list.append(params.copy())
        all_scores.append(score)

        return score

    # Run optimization
    if self.verbose:
        logger.info(f"Starting Bayesian optimization with {n_calls} evaluations...")
        logger.info(f"Optimizing parameters: {list(param_bounds.keys())}")
        logger.info(f"Observed groups: {list(self.observed_data.keys())}")
        logger.info(f"Simulation years: {len(self.years)}")

    self.n_calls = 0
    result = gp_minimize(
        objective,
        dimensions,
        n_calls=n_calls,
        n_initial_points=n_initial_points,
        random_state=random_state,
        verbose=False,
    )

    optimization_time = time.time() - start_time

    # Extract results
    best_params = {name: value for name, value in zip(param_names, result.x)}
    best_score = result.fun
    convergence = [np.min(all_scores[: i + 1]) for i in range(len(all_scores))]

    if self.verbose:
        logger.info(f"{'=' * 60}")
        logger.info("OPTIMIZATION COMPLETE")
        logger.info(f"{'=' * 60}")
        logger.info(f"Best score: {best_score:.6f}")
        logger.info("Best parameters:")
        for name, value in best_params.items():
            logger.info(f"  {name}: {value:.4f}")
        logger.info(f"Total evaluations: {self.n_calls}")
        logger.info(f"Optimization time: {optimization_time:.2f} seconds")
        logger.info(f"{'=' * 60}")

    return OptimizationResult(
        best_params=best_params,
        best_score=best_score,
        n_iterations=self.n_calls,
        convergence=convergence,
        all_params=all_params_list,
        all_scores=all_scores,
        optimization_time=optimization_time,
    )

    def log_likelihood(y_true: np.ndarray, y_pred: np.ndarray, sigma: float = 0.1) -> float:
    """Calculate negative log-likelihood (Gaussian).

    Parameters
    ----------
    y_true : np.ndarray
        Observed values
    y_pred : np.ndarray
        Predicted values
    sigma : float
        Standard deviation of measurement error

    Returns
    -------
    float
        Negative log-likelihood
    """
    n = len(y_true)
    return 0.5 * n * np.log(2 * np.pi * sigma**2) + np.sum((y_true - y_pred) ** 2) / (
        2 * sigma**2
    )

    def mean_absolute_percentage_error(y_true: np.ndarray, y_pred: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Calculate mean absolute percentage error.

    Parameters
    ----------
    y_true : np.ndarray
        Observed values
    y_pred : np.ndarray
        Predicted values

    Returns
    -------
    float
        Mean absolute percentage error
    """
    # Avoid division by zero
    mask = y_true != 0
    return np.mean(np.abs((y_true[mask] - y_pred[mask]) / y_true[mask])) * 100

    def normalized_root_mean_squared_error(y_true: np.ndarray, y_pred: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Calculate normalized root mean squared error.

    Parameters
    ----------
    y_true : np.ndarray
        Observed values
    y_pred : np.ndarray
        Predicted values

    Returns
    -------
    float
        Normalized RMSE
    """
    rmse = np.sqrt(np.mean((y_true - y_pred) ** 2))
    y_range = np.max(y_true) - np.min(y_true)
    if y_range <= 0:
        raise ValueError(
            "Cannot compute NRMSE: y_true has zero range (all values identical)"
        )
    return rmse / y_range

    def plot_fit(
    optimizer: EcosimOptimizer,
    params: Dict[str, float],
    save_path: Optional[str] = None,
):
    """Plot observed vs simulated biomass time series.

    Parameters
    ----------
    optimizer : EcosimOptimizer
        Optimizer instance with observed data
    params : dict
        Parameter values to simulate
    save_path : str, optional
        Path to save figure
    """
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

    # Run simulation
    simulated = optimizer._run_simulation(params)

    if simulated is None:
        logger.error("Simulation failed!")
        return None

    # Create figure
    n_groups = len(optimizer.observed_data)
    n_cols = min(3, n_groups)
    n_rows = (n_groups + n_cols - 1) // n_cols

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(n_rows, n_cols, figsize=(5 * n_cols, 4 * n_rows))
    if n_groups == 1:
        axes = np.array([axes])
    axes = axes.flatten()

    # Plot each group
    years = list(optimizer.years)
    for i, (group_idx, observed) in enumerate(optimizer.observed_data.items()):
        predicted = simulated[group_idx]
        group_name = optimizer.model.Group[group_idx]

        axes[i].plot(years, observed, "o-", label="Observed", linewidth=2, markersize=6)
        axes[i].plot(
            years, predicted, "s--", label="Simulated", linewidth=2, markersize=5
        )
        axes[i].set_xlabel("Year")
        axes[i].set_ylabel("Biomass")
        axes[i].set_title(f"{group_name} (Group {group_idx})")
        axes[i].legend()
        axes[i].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

        # Add metrics
        mse = mean_squared_error(observed, predicted)
        corr = np.corrcoef(observed, predicted)[0, 1]
        axes[i].text(
            0.05,
            0.95,
            f"MSE: {mse:.4f}\nCorr: {corr:.3f}",
            transform=axes[i].transAxes,
            verticalalignment="top",
            bbox=dict(boxstyle="round", facecolor="wheat", alpha=0.5),
        )

    # Hide unused subplots
    for i in range(n_groups, len(axes)):
        axes[i].axis("off")

    plt.tight_layout()

    if save_path:
        plt.savefig(save_path, dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")

    return fig

    def plot_optimization_results(
    result: OptimizationResult, save_path: Optional[str] = None
):
    """Plot optimization convergence and parameter distributions.

    Parameters
    ----------
    result : OptimizationResult
        Optimization results
    save_path : str, optional
        Path to save figure
    """
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4))

    # Convergence plot
    axes[0].plot(result.convergence, "b-", linewidth=2)
    axes[0].scatter(
        range(len(result.all_scores)),
        result.all_scores,
        c=result.all_scores,
        cmap="viridis",
        alpha=0.5,
        s=30,
    )
    axes[0].set_xlabel("Iteration")
    axes[0].set_ylabel("Best Objective Value")
    axes[0].set_title("Optimization Convergence")
    axes[0].grid(True, alpha=0.3)

    # Parameter evolution
    param_names = list(result.best_params.keys())
    n_params = len(param_names)

    if n_params <= 4:
        # Show all parameters if few enough
        for i, name in enumerate(param_names):
            values = [p[name] for p in result.all_params]
            axes[1].scatter(range(len(values)), values, label=name, alpha=0.6, s=30)
        axes[1].set_xlabel("Iteration")
        axes[1].set_ylabel("Parameter Value")
        axes[1].set_title("Parameter Evolution")
        axes[1].legend()
        axes[1].grid(True, alpha=0.3)
    else:
        # Show histogram of best parameters
        best_values = list(result.best_params.values())
        axes[1].barh(param_names, best_values, color="steelblue")
        axes[1].set_xlabel("Best Parameter Value")
        axes[1].set_title("Optimized Parameters")
        axes[1].grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis="x")

    plt.tight_layout()

    if save_path:
        plt.savefig(save_path, dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")

    return fig
